headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Botpress can egress broadly while Opik calls REST APIs, creating a default path for sensitive context to leave the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Botpress shows no io_surfaces and Opik only exposes REST API calls; neither profile shows a filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge that would let one agent inject instructions into the other by default.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects Botpress outputs into Opik prompts or tools, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between them, the pathway is no longer blocked.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe raw Botpress text into Opik prompts.
Add provenance tags before any handoff.
Review any future shared channel before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no network egress, but Opik has broad network egress and REST API calls. If they share a workspace or Botpress content is forwarded into Opik, sensitive context can leave the pair through Opik in default operation; the profiles do not show a blocking isolation mechanism.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are forwarded into Opik traces or API payloads, leakage becomes active.
IF both agents are placed on a shared workspace without isolation, file contents can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials.
Disable forwarding of raw prompts and attachments.
Redact secrets before any Opik ingestion.
Audit outbound REST destinations.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Opik can call REST APIs, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. Without a shared filesystem, git state, or shared OAuth scopes, direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk increases.
IF shared OAuth scopes are added for a mutable backend, concurrent writes can collide.
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories.
Avoid shared git branches.
Use a lock around any shared backend.
Keep OAuth scopes disjoint.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Opik is an observability/evaluation tool with REST API output, so it may consume Botpress-generated text as input. If Opik treats Botpress output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into logs, evaluations, or downstream actions; no verification control is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated answers are ingested into Opik evaluations without a verification step, cascading error is active.
IF Opik is configured to trigger alerts or actions from evaluated text, downstream impact expands.
mitigations: Require human review for Botpress-derived claims.
Mark Botpress outputs as untrusted in Opik.
Add a verification step before scoring or acting.
Limit Opik to read-only observation of Botpress.
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. Because Opik has broad egress while Botpress has none, a compliance issue could arise only if regulated data is routed into Opik; the other agent is not separately cited because no distinct compliance boundary is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed into Opik, compliance review is required.
IF a future deployment assigns different retention policies to the two agents, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into Opik.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Confirm data residency before deployment.
Keep Botpress outputs free of regulated fields.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
